• We propose a language independent neural end to end ASRs that can jointly perform language identification and speech recognition.

1) we propose a language independent hybrid attention/connectionist-temporal-classification architecture that can recognize speech and identify language, 2) we augment the output symbols of the model to include the union character sets of all the target languages, 3) we demonstrate the effectiveness of our model by training and evaluating on a multilingual database consisting of English (WSJ), Japanese (CSJ), Mandarin (HKUST), and European languages (Voxforge).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a single end-to-end neural architecture which jointly performs language identification (LID) and automatic speech recognition ( ASR) for multiple languages.
building end to-end ASR systems that can recognize speech without any linguistic information, and can jointly perform language identification (LI).
developing a monolithic multilanguage end-to-end ASR system that can be trained with a small number of labeled examples, without the need to develop language dependent acoustic models or lexicons.

We propose a language independent end to end architecture for joint language and speech recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
end to end ASRs can be built without linguistic information such as phoneme or grapheme dictionaries, and that they can be trained in a language independent manner.
we can train an end to end ASRs with a single architecture for multiple languages, without any linguistic knowledge.
we can build a monolithic multi-lingual ASR system by eliminating the need to use linguistic information (such as pronunciation dictionaries) and using a single model for multiple languages.
